name: Network Interfaces
purpose: Lists the network interfaces (physical and virtual adapters) available on the system and their last known configuration, including IP addressing, DHCP, and domain information.
key_fields: Interfaces\{adapter-GUID}\IPAddress / DhcpIPAddress / DhcpServer / DhcpDomain / DhcpSubnetMask / Domain
NetworkCards\{index}\ServiceName - the interface GUID, mapping this entry back to its Interfaces subkey
normal_baseline: A stable, expected set of adapter GUIDs (the built-in NIC plus any known VPN/virtual adapters) with IP/DHCP configuration consistent with the organization's known subnets.
anomalies: An unexpected virtual adapter appearing (VPN client, virtualization/tunneling software, or an attacker-installed network proxy tool) shortly before or during suspicious activity
An interface's DhcpDomain/Domain value not matching the organization's expected Active Directory domain, consistent with the host having connected to an untrusted or rogue network
A NetworkCards entry with no corresponding Interfaces GUID subkey, or vice versa, indicating adapter removal or registry inconsistency
anti_forensic_notes: These keys retain each interface's last-known configuration and subkeys may hold some prior DHCP-lease data depending on how the adapter has been reconfigured over time, but this is not a guaranteed complete history - a removed or re-enumerated (new GUID) adapter's earlier configuration can be lost entirely.
interpretation: The Interfaces key includes the last known IP address plus DHCP and domain information for both physical and virtual adapters, and its subkeys may hold some historical network data. The NetworkCards key provides more descriptive detail on each adapter's availability. The two keys are mapped to each other via the interface GUID value. This is unlikely to represent a fully complete view of every network the host has ever connected to.
